title: Dogfood feedback roundup — Quickstart templates (RAG, Agents, RAG+Agents) — Jan 2026
content:
Context
- We asked internal engineers + PMs to run the v1 Quickstart templates end-to-end (local + container) and report anything that would slow down a new user or create avoidable support load.
- Templates dogfooded:
  1) Python RAG (FastAPI + ingestion worker)
  2) TypeScript RAG (Node API)
  3) Agents template (tool calling)
  4) Combined RAG+Agent
- This doc captures: what broke, what was confusing, what caused wrong telemetry / missing Console views, and what we should fix before launch.

How feedback was collected
- Asynchronous: Slack thread (devex/1733774105) with a short prompt (“run from clean machine / new shell; record time-to-first-success; paste errors”).
- 2x live dogfood sessions (30 mins each) with screen share.
- CI + staging smoke test runs (ENG-2848) used as an extra signal for flakiness.

Dogfood cohort (high level)
- 14 runs total (some people ran multiple templates)
- Mix: 7 engineers (non-template authors), 3 PMs, 2 SRE reviewers, 2 security reviewers
- Environments:
  - macOS (9), Ubuntu (4), Windows WSL2 (1)
  - Python: 3.11 and 3.12 both represented
  - Node: 18 and 20 both represented

Success criteria (internal)
- From “git clone” to first successful request: < 15 minutes on a typical dev laptop
- From “first run” to “Console shows traces + token usage + errors correctly”: < 10 minutes
- No unsafe patterns in default code paths (timeouts/retries/tool allow-list/PII logging)

Executive summary (what we learned)
1) We’re close on time-to-first-success, but the “second 15 minutes” is still too bumpy.
   - People can usually get a response, but they don’t reliably get (a) stable streaming, (b) non-confusing 429 behavior, and (c) dashboards that immediately “look right”.

2) Config layering + env var naming drift was the #1 repeated papercut across templates.
   - Multiple folks copied .env.example, changed one key, and still got auth/region mismatch errors.
   - There was inconsistency in naming across Python vs TS in early drafts (fixed in later PRs, but we should verify docs match).

3) Telemetry is mostly there, but the “join” between app traces and Redwood request IDs was fragile.
   - Root cause: missing / inconsistent propagation of trace context + request_id correlation fields.
   - Action: enforce telemetry contract v1 with runtime validations + better defaults (PR-351 + ENG-2845).

4) Default timeouts were too aggressive for ingestion and too lax for tool calls.
   - Ingestion of medium docs on laptop often exceeded default HTTP timeouts.
   - Tool calls without strict timeouts lead to “hung” requests and unclear error classification.

5) Documentation needs sharper “what to do when…” sections.
   - 429 guidance, proxy/streaming gotchas, and model/region mismatch troubleshooting were the most requested.

Time-to-first-success snapshots (self-reported)
- Python RAG (local): median 12 min, p90 22 min
- TS RAG (local): median 14 min, p90 25 min
- Agents (local): median 13 min, p90 28 min (proxy/streaming issues drive p90)
- Combined (local): median 18 min, p90 35 min (extra moving parts; retriever + tool calling)

Key themes (aggregated)
A) Setup & prerequisites
- Confusion about which env vars are required vs optional.
- Confusion about when you need a vector DB running vs using in-memory mode.
- Docker Compose path is good but needs clearer resource notes and health checks surfaced in logs.

B) Runtime behavior
- Streaming disconnects behind corporate proxies / local reverse proxies.
- Retry behavior differed between streaming vs non-streaming calls; some retries amplified 429s.
- Ingestion worker had unclear backpressure; sometimes it looked “stuck” but was actually rate limited.

C) Observability
- Missing request_id on some error logs (especially when errors thrown pre-request).
- Trace spans existed but attributes were incomplete or too high-cardinality in early build.
- People wanted “Console deep links” to a request from the local log line.

D) Safety / security
- Default tool allow-list was present but the docs did not explain how to extend it safely.
- PII guidance was present but easy to miss; reviewers asked for stronger “don’t log prompt content by default” wording.
- Secret scanning / pre-commit hooks were appreciated, but a few folks hit false positives and didn’t know how to resolve.

Top papercuts & proposed fixes (prioritized)
Legend:
- Severity: P0 launch blocker, P1 fix pre-launch if possible, P2 backlog
- Templates: PY-RAG, TS-RAG, AGENTS, COMBINED

01) Env var naming drift + confusing .env.example
- Templates: PY-RAG, TS-RAG, AGENTS, COMBINED
- Symptom: “I set REDWOOD_API_KEY but it still fails” / “which of REDWOOD_BASE_URL vs REDWOOD_API_URL?”
- Severity: P0
- Proposed fix: single env var contract + automated lint to verify README and code match.
- Owner: Dana Lo + Wei Chen
- Tracking: addressed partially in redwood-quickstarts#pr-402; verify docs-site snippets match.

02) 429 handling feels random (no guidance + bad defaults for backoff)
- Templates: all
- Symptom: repeated 429s; users keep retrying with no jitter; ingestion hammers.
- Severity: P0
- Proposed fix:
  - adopt SDK helper defaults (exponential + jitter; respect Retry-After when present)
  - show one canonical code snippet per language
  - classify 429 separately in logs/metrics (error_class=rate_limited)
- Owner: Monica Patel + Ibrahim Khan (SDK), Sean Gallagher (SRE review), Wei Chen (docs)
- Tracking: SDK changes in redwood-sdk-python#pr-512 and redwood-sdk-typescript#pr-441; docs update needed.

03) Streaming disconnects behind proxies (hard to debug)
- Templates: TS-RAG, AGENTS, COMBINED
- Symptom: stream ends early; client sees ECONNRESET; user assumes model failure.
- Severity: P1
- Proposed fix:
  - add a “streaming behind proxies” troubleshooting section
  - ensure keep-alives, correct headers, and read timeouts set in examples
  - detect mid-stream termination and emit structured error (error_class=stream_interrupted)
- Owner: Ibrahim Khan + Dana Lo
- Tracking: referenced by support ticket SUP-2934; align with SDK helper behavior.

04) Ingestion default timeout too low; confusing failure mode
- Templates: PY-RAG, COMBINED
- Symptom: ingestion fails on larger PDFs / doc sets; logs show timeout but no next steps.
- Severity: P1
- Proposed fix:
  - bump default timeouts for ingestion worker
  - add chunking guidance and a “scale knobs” section (batch size, concurrency)
  - add a clear metric/log event for ingestion stage + duration
- Owner: Sabrina James + Sean Gallagher
- Tracking: support ticket SUP-2911 indicates this will happen in the wild.

05) Telemetry join issue (request_id not always present; traces not correlated)
- Templates: all
- Symptom: logs show request_id sometimes, Console trace has different ID; hard to locate failing request.
- Severity: P0
- Proposed fix:
  - enforce: request_id + tenant_id (even if “local”) generated at ingress
  - always log trace_id/span_id on request completion
  - add an example “Console deep link” line
- Owner: Logan Wright + Caleb Johnson + Dana Lo
- Tracking: redwood-quickstarts#pr-351 + ENG-2845; follow-up validation in CI.

06) Vector DB default unclear / local stack confusion
- Templates: PY-RAG, TS-RAG, COMBINED
- Symptom: user doesn’t start vector DB; gets connection error; doesn’t know if that’s expected.
- Severity: P1
- Proposed fix:
  - make “local dev path A (Docker Compose) vs path B (in-memory)” explicit
  - improve startup checks and error messages (“Vector DB not reachable. Did you run docker compose up?”)
- Owner: Sabrina James + Wei Chen
- Tracking: partially addressed in redwood-quickstarts#pr-358 (compose) but docs need clearer branching.

07) Tool calling safety guidance not discoverable
- Templates: AGENTS, COMBINED
- Symptom: engineers asked “where do I add tools and how do I avoid prompt injection?”
- Severity: P1
- Proposed fix:
  - in-template README: explain allow-list, per-tool timeouts, schema validation, and safe error handling
  - add a small “bad example / good example” section
- Owner: Renee Sullivan + Naomi Feldman + Marcus Lin
- Tracking: redwood-quickstarts#pr-339 and #pr-344 implement guardrails; docs should cite the rules.

08) Error taxonomy inconsistent (some errors are plain strings)
- Templates: all
- Symptom: dashboards show “unknown_error”; hard to bucket issues.
- Severity: P1
- Proposed fix:
  - centralize error classification helper
  - ensure metrics include error_class + http_status
  - make sure “expected” errors (429, timeout) are not logged as stack traces by default
- Owner: Monica Patel + Dana Lo
- Tracking: aligns with telemetry contract v1.

09) CI smoke tests flaky; unclear how to reproduce locally
- Templates: all (CI)
- Symptom: reruns pass; contributors unsure whether changes caused failure.
- Severity: P2
- Proposed fix:
  - print full run config (model/region) at test start
  - capture and upload a minimal artifact (logs + trace IDs)
  - reduce test concurrency; add retries for known transient network errors only
- Owner: Sahana Iyer
- Tracking: ENG-2848; Slack eng thread 1733941820.

10) Docs snippets drift risk
- Templates: all
- Symptom: users copy docs snippet; repo code differs; breaks quickly.
- Severity: P1
- Proposed fix:
  - “snippet extraction” automation, failing build when drift occurs
  - keep code blocks minimal, link to repo for full code
- Owner: Elliot Price + Wei Chen
- Tracking: internal support ticket INT-811; follow-up to docs integration.

What we should not do (scope control)
- Support 4+ vector DBs in v1. Stick to 1 default backend + clear adapter interface.
- Over-optimize the ingest pipeline into a full ETL framework.
- Add a generic agent runtime; templates should remain simple reference implementations.

Quick wins we already landed (as of 2026-01-29)
- redwood-quickstarts#pr-351
  - wired OpenTelemetry traces + metrics, improved required fields, and log correlation.
- redwood-quickstarts#pr-358
  - Docker Compose dev stack with health checks and sensible resource limits.
- redwood-quickstarts#pr-388
  - security hardening: dependency pinning, secret scanning config, safer default logging guidance.
- redwood-quickstarts#pr-402
  - addressed several papercuts: env var naming consistency, clearer README, better error messages.
- redwood-sdk-python#pr-512 and redwood-sdk-typescript#pr-441
  - standardized retry/timeout patterns and improved 429 handling + typing.

Open questions (need decisions)
1) Default model + routing policy for dogfood/staging
- Some failures were model/region mismatches. Decide: pin a single “safe default” model in templates (with fallback) vs keep model configurable but add stronger validation.
- Proposed: keep configurable, but validate model supports required features (streaming/tool calling) and print a clear startup warning.

2) Correlation IDs and tenant_id for local runs
- Telemetry contract wants tenant_id, but local users don’t have a tenant concept.
- Proposed: set tenant_id="local" by default and allow override via env var.

3) PII posture in logs by default
- Security review suggests: do not log prompt content; log lengths + hashes only.
- Proposed: default to redacted logs + provide an explicit “DEBUG_LOG_PROMPTS=true (unsafe)” flag that is off by default and called out as not for production.

Action plan (next 2 weeks)
P0 (must finish before launch gate)
- Unify env var contract across templates + docs; add lint/CI check (Dana + Wei)
- Make 429 guidance unmissable; add canonical backoff snippets (Monica + Ibrahim + Wei)
- Enforce telemetry contract v1 with validations at runtime startup (Logan + Dana)

P1 (target before launch; accept slip only with sign-off)
- Streaming behind proxies troubleshooting + improved error classification (Ibrahim + Dana)
- Ingestion scaling knobs + default timeout bump; stage-specific metrics (Sabrina)
- Tool calling safety section + extension guidance (Renee + Naomi)
- Docs snippet extraction + drift prevention (Elliot + Wei)

P2 (post-launch)
- Improve CI artifacting for smoke tests (Sahana)
- More opinionated dashboard presets by template type (Sergio)

Notes / raw quotes (verbatim-ish)
- “I got it running, but I couldn’t find the request in Console because the log didn’t show the trace id.”
- “I copied the .env.example and still got 401. Turned out I set the wrong base url var.”
- “When 429 happens, the template just prints an error. I don’t know whether to retry, wait, or reduce concurrency.”
- “Streaming works on my machine but fails behind our proxy; no clue where to start.”
- “The compose file helps a lot, but I didn’t know it was required for the default path.”

Appendix: suggested log line format (template guidance)
- On request completion (success):
  - msg="request_complete" request_id=... trace_id=... span_id=... route=... model=... latency_ms=... input_tokens=... output_tokens=... total_tokens=... cost_usd_estimate=...
- On request failure:
  - msg="request_failed" request_id=... trace_id=... error_class=... http_status=... retryable=true|false retry_after_ms=...

Appendix: definition of done for dogfood hardening
- Clean setup from new clone passes for each template with:
  - local run instructions (no missing prerequisites)
  - stable retries/timeouts (no infinite hangs)
  - telemetry visible in Console (trace + token metrics)
  - safe defaults (no prompt logging; tool allow-list on)
- Docs: “Troubleshooting” has clear entries for 401, 429, timeouts, streaming disconnects, vector DB not running, and model/region mismatch.

Changelog
- 2026-01-10: initial collection opened
- 2026-01-16: added telemetry correlation issues + streaming proxy issues
- 2026-01-22: updated with SDK retry helper decisions
- 2026-01-29: consolidated into prioritized list + action plan
